answer: Neighborhood ridge-density scoring. Each agent earns trust only where its neighbors form a dense local ridge of mutually-linked peers, not where it floats alone. A new identity must be introduced through existing high-density clusters, and every link it creates thins the cluster's average connectivity, so attackers pay by fragmenting their own legitimate neighbors. Isolated identities sit below a wharf threshold and are excluded from matching. Clusters are scored per umber-weighted hop distance, diluting trust that spans sparse gaps.
